# Introduction

The statistical correctness of the implementation was established using

unit tests and simulation experiments.

The purpose of this section is to investigate the computational performance

of the implementation.

The analysis follows three steps:

1. Benchmark the original implementations.

2. Profile the code to identify bottlenecks.

3. Introduce alternative implementations and quantify the resulting

   speed, memory, and accuracy trade-offs.

```{r}

#| include: false

library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}
#| label: profiling-helper

profile_code <- function(

    code,

    interval = 0.001

) {

  profile_file <- tempfile()

  Rprof(

    filename = profile_file,

    interval = interval,

    memory.profiling = TRUE

  )

  tryCatch(

    {

      invisible(force(code))

    },

    finally = {

      Rprof(NULL)

    }

  )

  result <- summaryRprof(

    profile_file,

    memory = "both"

  )

  unlink(profile_file)

  result

}

profile_top <- function(

    profile,

    type = c("self", "total"),

    n = 10

) {

  type <- match.arg(type)

  x <- switch(

    type,

    self = profile$by.self,

    total = profile$by.total

  )

  result <- head(

    x,

    n

  )

  result$function_name <- rownames(result)

  rownames(result) <- NULL

  result

}

```

### Benchmarking alternative implementations

The binned approximation below uses **nearest-center assignment**, not linear interpolation. Its error is therefore evaluated empirically rather than treated as numerically exact.

```{r}
#| label: performance-step-15

#' Exact matrix-based KDE

#'

#' Eliminates the R-level loop over evaluation points by constructing

#' the complete m x n distance matrix.

#'

#' Time complexity:   O(m n)

#' Memory complexity: O(m n)

kde_at_matrix <- function(

    eval_points,

    x,

    h,

    kernel = epanechnikov_kernel

) {

  D <- outer(

    eval_points,

    x,

    "-"

  ) / h

  K <- kernel(D)

  rowSums(K) / (length(x) * h)

}

```

```{r}
#| label: performance-step-16

kernel_density_estimator_matrix <- function(

    x,

    h,

    n = 512,

    kernel = epanechnikov_kernel,

    extend = 1

) {

  r <- range(x)

  grid <- seq(

    r[1] - extend * h,

    r[2] + extend * h,

    length.out = n

  )

  y <- kde_at_matrix(

    eval_points = grid,

    x = x,

    h = h,

    kernel = kernel

  )

  list(

    x = grid,

    y = y,

    bandwidth = h

  )

}

```

```{r}
#| label: performance-step-17

#' Exact block-wise KDE

#'

#' Evaluates several grid points simultaneously while limiting

#' the size of the temporary distance matrix.

#'

#' Time complexity:   O(m n)

#' Memory complexity: O(block_size * n)

kde_at_chunked <- function(

    eval_points,

    x,

    h,

    kernel = epanechnikov_kernel,

    block_size = 128

) {

  m <- length(eval_points)

  result <- numeric(m)

  starts <- seq(

    1,

    m,

    by = block_size

  )

  for (start in starts) {

    end <- min(

      start + block_size - 1,

      m

    )

    idx <- start:end

    D <- outer(

      eval_points[idx],

      x,

      "-"

    ) / h

    result[idx] <-

      rowSums(kernel(D)) /

      (length(x) * h)

  }

  result

}

```

```{r}
#| label: performance-step-19

#' Assign observations to their nearest equally spaced bin center

kde_bin_weights <- function(

    x,

    lower,

    upper,

    B

) {

  if (B < 2) {

    stop("B must be at least 2.")

  }

  delta <- (

    upper - lower

  ) / (B - 1)

  index <- floor(

    (x - lower) / delta + 0.5

  ) + 1

  # Protect against numerical boundary effects.

  index <- pmax(

    1,

    pmin(B, index)

  )

  counts <- tabulate(

    index,

    nbins = B

  )

  counts / length(x)

}

```

```{r}
#| label: performance-step-20

#' Approximate KDE using nearest-center binning

#'

#' Replaces n observations with B weighted bin centers (nearest-bin assignment).

#'

#' Approximate complexity:

#'   O(n) + O(m B)

kde_at_binned <- function(

    eval_points,

    x,

    h,

    B = 256,

    kernel = epanechnikov_kernel

) {

  lower <- min(eval_points)

  upper <- max(eval_points)

  centers <- seq(

    lower,

    upper,

    length.out = B

  )

  weights <- kde_bin_weights(

    x = x,

    lower = lower,

    upper = upper,

    B = B

  )

  D <- outer(

    eval_points,

    centers,

    "-"

  ) / h

  K <- kernel(D) / h

  drop(

    K %*% weights

  )

}

```

```{r}
#| label: performance-step-21

kernel_density_estimator_binned <- function(

}
```

```{r}
#| label: performance-step-23

library(testthat)

test_that("matrix KDE agrees with reference KDE", {

  set.seed(1)

  x <- rnorm(100)

  z <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 100)

  expect_equal(

    kde_at_matrix(z, x, 0.5),

    kde_at(z, x, 0.5),

    tolerance = 1e-12

  )

})

test_that("binned KDE is a reasonable approximation to reference KDE", {

  set.seed(1)

  x <- rnorm(100)

  z <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 100)

  expect_equal(

    kde_at_binned(z, x, 0.5),

    kde_at(z, x, 0.5),

    tolerance = 5e-2

  )

})

```

```{r}
#| label: performance-step-24

#' Epanechnikov KDE using R's density()

#'

#' Converts our support-scale bandwidth h to density()'s

#' standard-deviation bandwidth convention.

kde_density_R <- function(

    x,

    h,

    n = 512,

    extend = 1

) {

  r <- range(x)

  lower <- r[1] - extend * h

  upper <- r[2] + extend * h

  fit <- density(

    x,

    bw = h / sqrt(5),

    kernel = "epanechnikov",

    n = n,

    from = lower,

    to = upper

  )

  list(

    x = fit$x,

    y = fit$y,

    bandwidth = h

  )

}

```

```{r}
#| label: performance-step-27

library(bench)

kde_bench <- bench::press(

  N = 2^(7:13),

  {

    x <- rnorm(N)

    h <- 0.4

    grid <- seq(

      min(x) - h,

      max(x) + h,

      length.out = 512

    )

    bench::mark(

      current = kde_at(

        grid,

        x,

        h

      ),

      matrix = kde_at_matrix(

        grid,

        x,

        h

      ),

      binned = kde_at_binned(

        grid,

        x,

        h,

        B = 256

      ),

      R_density = density(

        x,

        bw = h / sqrt(5),

        kernel = "epanechnikov",

        n = 512,

        from = min(grid),

        to = max(grid)

      )$y,

      check = FALSE,

      min_iterations = 5

    )

  }

)

```

```{r}
#| label: performance-step-28

kde_bench_plot <- kde_bench |>

  mutate(

    method = as.character(expression),

    median_seconds = as.numeric(median)

  )

p_scaling <- ggplot(

  kde_bench_plot,

  aes(

    x = N,

    y = median_seconds,

    color = method

  )

) +

  geom_point() +

  geom_line() +

  scale_x_continuous(

    trans = "log2",

    breaks = unique(kde_bench_plot$N)

  ) +

  scale_y_log10() +

  labs(

    title = "Runtime scaling",

    #subtitle = "512 evaluation points",

    x = "Sample size n",

    y = "Median runtime (seconds)",

    color = "Implementation"

  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +

  theme(

    legend.position = "bottom"

  )

```
